Humanities 111 was one of my favourite courses, where I learned a lot and got an A, whereas this one (Hum112) is the worst one. I am sorry to say that even though I did all the readings and listened to all the classes carefully, I didn't learn much from this course and got a poor grade. I think the instructor should reconsider his teaching methods. We almost never opened the texts and analyzed important passages during classes. He just gave general and trivial information about the texts, and I think the class discussions were very inefficient, and it distracted the class from the main idea of the texts (the discussions could have been managed better). I strongly think that he should stick closer to the texts instead of losing in unnecessary details, since this is a course aimed at introducing the fundamental ideas and texts from history to the students, not necessarily from a relevant field. In the last two weeks, we studied the "instructor's favourite poems". I don't think studying "instructor's favourite poems" aligns with the syllabus of the course. 
His grading is really poor. He doesn't give clear feedback, and the expectations for the assignments aren't clear. For instance, I don't understand why I lost points in the course projects because the reasons the instructor gave as feedback weren't included in the assignment description. He should clearly express what he expects from an assignment so that we can understand why we lost those points, and there is no ambiguity. There is no grading criteria, he just deducts points to his liking. The instructor should change his grading method. I suppose he thinks like "Oh, this isn't a perfect paper, so I should deduct 2 points." This is a course where even 2 points can reduce your letter grade, and those 2 points add up with each assignment. Thus, I strongly recommend taking this course from a different instructor. Sadly, I will need to retake this course. What a waste of time and energy :(
